entry.title: Paint Box of Vizier Amenemope
entry.blurb: This paint box was made in Egypt more than 3,000 years ago.

source.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust

facts: Conservators identified the pigments using X-ray diffraction, a process that helps them determine the minerals that make up each color.
The paint box belonged to a man named Amenemope (say: ah-men-em-oh-pee) who advised the pharaoh (king).
He probably used it for fun, and it may have been buried with him when he died.

candidate.title: Paint Box of Vizier Amenemope
candidate.medium: boxwood with inscription inlaid in Egyptian blue
candidate.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust
candidate.description: This paint box was made in Egypt more than 3,000 years ago. It includes five pots of color, each made of different minerals. Conservators identified the pigments using X-ray diffraction, a process that helps them determine the minerals that make up each color. The paint box belonged to a man named Amenemope (say: ah-men-em-oh-pee) who advised the pharaoh (king). He probably used it for fun, and it may have been buried with him when he died. The coffin panel on view nearby was made for a different man named Amenemope hundreds of years later. Imagine you are painting a picture for a king! Which colors would you use? What would you paint? Painting was a popular and time-honored pastime among the upper classes in Egypt.
candidate.culture: Egypt, New Kingdom (1540–1069 BCE), Dynasty 18, reign of Amenhotep II (1425–1400 BCE)
